notes:
CRM-style notes / negotiation log:
- Summary: Monospace wants guaranteed production-grade Dedicated pool for personalization + reranking. Primary ask: minimum sustained throughput with deterministic concurrency caps and clearly defined burst policy.
- Customer requested SLA targets (requested by Monospace):
  * Sustained minimum: 15,000 tokens/sec (aggregate, input+output) measured at 1-min windows, 95th percentile monthly
  * Concurrency cap: support for 350 concurrent inference sessions with per-session soft timeouts
  * Burst allowance: up to 2.5x sustained for up to 10 minutes per hour (auto-burst), plus manual one-off bursts for seasonal events (Black Friday) subject to advance notice
  * Latency SLOs: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 220ms for short-form prompts (<256 tokens); longer sequences need separate baseline
- Redwood initial proposal (Julian):
  * Baseline guarantee: 12,000 tokens/sec sustained, scaling to 24,000 tokens/sec with burst window (1-min average) using dedicated reserve + autoscale buffer
  * Concurrency guidance: 250 concurrent sessions per 8-GPU reserve (A100-class equiv); customer workload maps to ~10 GPUs for baseline with buffer for GC/maintenance
  * Burst policy: 2x sustained for 15 minutes per hour default; manual bursts available via reserved 'burst credits' purchased as add-on. Technical caveats: cold-starts for new model versions not covered unless pre-warmed.
  * Measurement and billing: tokens defined as input + output; measurement windows: 1-minute, aggregated by customer tenant, 95th percentile used for SLA checks; billing to include sustained commit + overage for bursts if over purchased credits.
- PoC findings (Mar 2-8):
  * Sustained throughput at baseline config: ~13.2k tokens/sec (1-min avg) across test traffic profile (50/50 short/long prompts)
negotiation_points: Monospace pushing for 15k sustained; Redwood countered with 12k guaranteed + documented burst mechanics
Measurement: customer insists on 5-min window; Redwood prefers 1-min for accuracy — legal asked for explicit definition
Burst credits: customer requests 'seasonal' unlimited bursts for an annual fee; Redwood proposed capped purchased credits
Penalties: Monospace wants service credits starting at 1% invoice per 1% shortfall; Redwood proposed tiered credits capped at 25%
